sections.label: Overview
sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Thēseus** ​(*theseus*) ‌— Heroism, ‌Athens, ​Labours ​· ​The Gatherer ​(from ​τίθημι) ‌— belongs ​to ​the ‌Greek ​tradition, where ‌it ​is ‌catalogued ​under the ​domain ​"Heroism, ​Athens, Labours". ​The ‌name ​means ‌"The Gatherer ​(from ‌τίθημι)"[^1].

​**Thēseus** ‌belongs to ​the ‌Greek ​tradition, where ​it ‌is ‌associated ‌with heroism, ​athens, ​labours.[^2]

‌PuniCodex ​restores the ​name ‌as ​**Thēseus** and ​serves ‌its ​temple ‌at [theseus.com](https://punicodex.com/theseus/). ​The ​original ​carries ​both stress ‌and ‌vowel ​length, and ‌exactly ​one ​historically ‌valid Unicode ‌restoration ‌exists, ‌which ​places the ‌name ​in ​Tier 1. ​The ‌plain ​ASCII ​form *theseus* ​survives ‌as ​a ​modern convenience ​imposed ‌by ​the early ‌domain-name ​system; ‌the ​restoration, not ‌the ‌fallback, ​is ​the form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete[^3].

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, ASCII constraint, Unicode restoration, name variations, tier classification.
sections.body:
The ​name is ‌attested in ‌Greek as ​**Θησεύς**. Etymologically ​it means ​"The Gatherer ​(from τίθημι)"[^1].

​The reconstructed ‌proto-form ​is *dʰeh₁-* ​(proto-indo-european, "to ‌put, to ​place"). Greek ‌Θησεύς, popularly ​derived from ‌τίθημι 'to ​set, to ​place'; ​the Athenian ​hero who ​slew the ‌Minotaur and ​unified Attica.

‌The ASCII ​form *theseus* ‌survives ​only because ‌the early ​domain-name system ‌could not ​carry diacritics; ​it is ‌a technological ‌compromise, not ‌an ​ancient spelling. ​The Unicode ‌restoration **Thēseus** ​recovers the ​vowel length ‌of the ​original directly ​in the ‌address ​bar. The ‌original carries ​both stress ​and vowel ​length, and ​exactly one ‌historically valid ‌Unicode restoration ​exists, ‌which places ​the name ​in Tier ‌1.

The ‌letter-by-letter transformation ‌runs:

- ‌**t** → ​**T** — ‌Tau
​- **h** ​→ **h** ​— Theta
‌- **e** ​→ **ē** ​— Eta: ​long epsilon
‌- ​**s** → ​**s** — ​Sigma
- ‌**e** → ​**e** — ‌Short epsilon
​- **u** ‌→ **u** ​— ‌Upsilon
- ‌**s** → ​**s** — ​Sigma

The ​canonical temple ​for this ‌name is ‌served at ​**theseus.com**[^2].

sections.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation ‌of ​the ​name is ​**/theseus/** ​— ​Greek ‌Reconstruction.[^1]

​Phoneme ​by ‌phoneme:

​- ‌**T** ​— Initial ‌character ​of ​the ​restored ​form ​Thēseus.
‌- ​**hēseus** ‌— Remainder ​of ‌the ​name, ‌preserving ​the ‌distinctive ​marks ​of ‌the ‌Greek tradition.

‌For ​the ​modern ‌speaker, ​the ​closest ‌approximation ​is: ​'THESEUS' ‌— pronounce ​the ‌restored ​form ​with ​attention ​to ‌the ‌preserved ​diacritics ‌and length.

​Kindred ​and ‌historical ‌forms ‌of ‌the ​name:

‌- ​**Greek** ​— Thēseus, ​the ‌restored ​Unicode ​form ​of ‌the ​name

​Thēseus ​is Tier ‌1 ​because ‌the ​Greek ‌form ​preserves ‌distinctive ‌features ​that ​ASCII loses: ​stress, ​length, ‌or ‌special ​characters.

sections.body:
The ​stories of ‌**Thēseus** ‌circulate within ​the ​Greek corpus, ​where ​the ​figure embodies ‌heroism, ​athens, labours.[^1]

​### ‌Primary Attestation ​(Sources)

‌Thēseus is ​attested ‌in the ​canonical ​Greek sources ​as ​a figure ​associated ‌with ​heroism, athens, ‌labours.[^2]

​### Name ‌and ​Meaning (Etymology)

‌The ​name means ‌"The ​Gatherer (from ​τίθημι)" ‌and reflects ‌the ‌figure's role ​in ​the ‌tradition. **Thēseus** ​is ​the Athenian ‌hero ​who slew ​the ‌Minotaur in ​the ‌Cretan Labyrinth ​and ​unified Attica ​under ​Athens. With ‌Ariadne's ‌thread ​he navigated ‌the ​maze, then ​abandoned ‌her on ‌Naxos—an ‌act that ‌later ​tradition both ‌criticized ​and mythologized.[^1] ​His ​career bridges ‌the ​age ​of monsters ​and ‌the age ​of ​civic law. ​His ‌later deeds—including ​the ‌battle with ​the ‌Centaurs, the ​Calydonian ‌boar hunt, ‌and ​the ​Amazonomachy—made him ​the ​paradigmatic civic ‌hero ‌of classical ​Athens.[^2]
